concepts.definition: A benefit with Guarantee Credit and Savings Credit components; the captured entitlement conditions, household rules and financial assessment must be read together.
concepts.label: State Pension Credit

concepts.definition: The Guarantee Credit component of Pension Credit has a financial assessment and additional-amount dependencies distinct from Savings Credit.
concepts.label: Guarantee Credit

concepts.definition: The Savings Credit component has separate conditions and calculations. Do not treat its thresholds as the Guarantee Credit calculation.
concepts.label: Savings Credit

concepts.definition: The question label State Pension requires regime resolution. DMG 74001 distinguishes new State Pension from the earlier Retirement Pension regime.
concepts.label: State Pension

concepts.definition: DMG chapter 74 distinguishes the post-6 April 2016 pensionable-age regime and its full-rate and transitional branches.
concepts.label: New State Pension

concepts.definition: DMG 74001 names Retirement Pension as the legislative name for the earlier State Pension regime and routes readers to chapter 75.
concepts.label: Retirement Pension

concepts.definition: Reaching pensionable age is a condition separate from contribution records, a valid claim, applicable regime and payment date.
concepts.label: State Pension age

concepts.definition: PIP has daily living and mobility components. ADM supplies its own age, entitlement and transition guidance; AA or DLA rules cannot simply be transferred to PIP.
concepts.label: Personal Independence Payment

concepts.definition: This component is named in the Carer’s Allowance qualifying-benefit list and the Pension Credit severe-disability additional-amount conditions; the other conditions remain material.
concepts.label: PIP daily living component

concepts.definition: PIP mobility is distinct from daily living. The captured upper-age guidance contains restrictions on later mobility changes.
concepts.label: PIP mobility component

concepts.definition: DLA has component-specific age conditions and separate transition arrangements towards PIP; jurisdiction and existing-award status require resolution.
concepts.label: Disability Living Allowance

concepts.definition: Attendance Allowance is a distinct benefit named in qualifying-benefit and overlap provisions; it is not interchangeable with PIP, DLA or a Constant Attendance Allowance scheme.
concepts.label: Attendance Allowance

concepts.definition: The captured IIDB guidance specifies industrial accident/disease and disablement conditions; distinct supplements and overlap questions must be assessed separately.
concepts.label: Industrial Injuries Disablement Benefit

concepts.definition: The industrial-injuries CAA route has its own disablement and attendance conditions. A war-pensions allowance must not silently be equated with this scheme.
concepts.label: Industrial Injuries Constant Attendance Allowance

concepts.definition: The staff wording War Pensions Constant Allowance is retained as an unresolved scheme-name proposal. Overlap guidance names service-pensions instruments separately from industrial-injuries CAA.
concepts.label: War Pensions Constant Attendance Allowance

concepts.definition: Reduced Earnings Allowance has a separate pension-age and historical transition context; those rules cannot be transferred to IIDB merely because both concern industrial injury.
concepts.label: Reduced Earnings Allowance

concepts.definition: SDA is a distinct legacy benefit with captured closure and continuation conditions. The acronym may instead be used informally for a Pension Credit disability addition and is deliberately ambiguous.
concepts.label: Severe Disablement Allowance

concepts.definition: Navigation to the Pension Credit additional amount for people who are severely disabled. The captured guidance identifies separate no-partner and partner branches in DMG 78034 and 78045. The permanent-care-home paragraph 78088 is headed Claimants who have no partner (including self-funders) and requires all its conditions to be satisfied. This additional amount is distinct from the Severe Disablement Allowance benefit described in DMG 57001. This overview does not set out the full qualifying conditions or a consolidated current-law rule.
concepts.label: Pension Credit severe-disability additional amount

concepts.definition: Carer’s Allowance has caring, age, employment, education and residence/presence conditions. Actual payment, underlying entitlement and effects on other awards are separate questions.
concepts.label: Carer’s Allowance

concepts.definition: The additional amount for carers refers to entitlement to Carer’s Allowance or being treated as satisfying qualifying conditions, with exclusions and continuation rules.
concepts.label: Pension Credit carer additional amount

concepts.definition: Housing Benefit income treatment in Pension Credit is distinct from eligibility for Housing Benefit and from a Pension Credit housing-cost additional amount.
concepts.label: Housing Benefit

concepts.definition: JSA needs contributory, income-based or New Style regime resolution before entitlement, income and overlap rules are selected.
concepts.label: Jobseeker’s Allowance

concepts.definition: The contributory JSA variant must be distinguished from the income-based and New Style regimes and from payment deductions.
concepts.label: Contributory JSA

concepts.definition: Income-based JSA is a distinct legacy means-tested variant; broad JSA wording does not establish its applicability.
concepts.label: Income-based JSA

concepts.definition: New Style JSA has its own ADM amount and pension-payment rules; regime and claim date must be resolved.
concepts.label: New Style JSA

concepts.definition: ESA needs contributory, income-related or New Style regime resolution before the correct entitlement and payment rules can be selected.
concepts.label: Employment and Support Allowance

concepts.definition: The contributory ESA variant must be distinguished from the income-related and New Style regimes.
concepts.label: Contributory ESA

concepts.definition: Income-related ESA is a distinct legacy means-tested variant; broad ESA wording alone cannot select it.
concepts.label: Income-related ESA

concepts.definition: The ADM ESA introduction defines the source’s post-abolition-of-income-related-ESA scope and routes transitional questions separately.
concepts.label: New Style ESA

concepts.definition: Temporary absence, permanent residence abroad and exportability are separate benefit-specific questions; duration, purpose, destination and dates matter.
concepts.label: Absence abroad

concepts.definition: Permanent and temporary care-home stays require different Pension Credit household and component checks. DMG 78088 is under the heading Claimants who have no partner (including self-funders): all severe-disability-addition conditions still apply, including actual qualifying-benefit receipt. One partner entering permanently and both partners living permanently in a home require the separate DMG 77128–77130 household branches. Funding alone does not determine the whole credit.
concepts.label: Permanent care-home residence

concepts.definition: Pension Credit couple status requires the DMG 77013 definition and household facts. Temporary absence, one partner entering a care home permanently, both partners living there, and mixed-age status are distinct conditional branches. Shared accommodation alone does not establish a shared household; the DMG 77130 factors are non-exhaustive and none alone decides the question.
concepts.label: Partner and household membership

concepts.definition: Actual and notional capital, ownership, valuation and disregards precede any deemed-income assessment. Savings is not a complete capital definition.
concepts.label: Capital

concepts.definition: Named income types and individual disregards must be read with their scopes; inclusion in a list alone does not determine an award.
concepts.label: Income other than earnings

concepts.definition: The source separates entitlement conditions, Guarantee Credit, Savings Credit, income/capital and additions. These dependencies do not constitute an executable award calculator.
concepts.label: Pension Credit assessment inputs

concepts.definition: Historical weekly figures need an agreed period, component and household scope; an uprating memo can route to a separate schedule without containing all rates.
concepts.label: Dated benefit rates

concepts.definition: Pension Credit additional amounts have separate qualifying conditions; they are not automatic passported entitlements.
concepts.label: Additional amounts

concepts.definition: Concurrent entitlement, income treatment, overlapping payment, qualifying-benefit links and effects on another person’s award are different relationships.
concepts.label: Benefit interaction

concepts.definition: One person caring for several people is distinct from several carers for one person. DMG 60044 refers to care for one qualifying person and must be read with 60043.
concepts.label: Caring for several people

concepts.definition: A general eligibility question requires benefit-specific conditions and scope; claiming, entitlement and payment are distinct.
concepts.label: Conditions of entitlement

concepts.definition: An additional-benefit question requires a bounded inventory and each benefit or component’s own conditions. A qualifying-benefit link does not establish automatic entitlement.
concepts.label: Additional benefits or supplements

concepts.definition: Meeting entitlement conditions is distinct from the amount payable or deductions from payment. The precise distinction depends on the selected benefit and source scope.
concepts.label: Entitlement

concepts.definition: A payment, reduction or overlap rule is not by itself proof that underlying entitlement ends or survives. Inspect the benefit-specific wording and conditions.
concepts.label: Payment and payability

aliases: both partners in a care home
concepts.definition: DMG 77013 defines a couple; DMG 77102 explains household as a domestic establishment, not merely a building. Under DMG 77128, one partner entering a care home permanently is treated as no longer in the same household. Where both enter permanently, the decision maker must establish whether they remain one household on the facts. DMG 77129–77130 require reasonable independence and responsibility in running a domestic establishment; the seven factors are non-exhaustive and none is decisive alone. DMG 78089 says each may claim when household membership ends, not that an award automatically follows. Temporary absence is a separate branch.
concepts.label: Pension Credit household separation and care-home residence

additional_sources.anchor: which the award is first paid

concepts.definition: Bounded reading of the captured lower-rate branch for a claimant with no partner. DMG 78034–78036 set receipt, residence and caring conditions and the stated transitional-protection exception. In DMG 78057, Carer’s Allowance or Universal Credit including the carer element, in respect of caring for the claimant or partner, must actually be in payment before it affects entitlement to this additional amount. That is not a universal cash-payment test for disability benefits: DMG 78060 treats specified disability benefits as received for periods before an award is made but in respect of which it is awarded, or periods not covered by an award but with payment in lieu of an award, and treats CA or UC including the carer element as not received before its first payment. Its separate patient provision expressly concerns a claimant who has a partner and must not be transferred to a no-partner care-home case. Under the no-partner heading, DMG 78088 requires all conditions to remain satisfied; funding status alone does not settle them. Read these captured passages with the separate dated changes in memos 02/25, 06/25 and 01/26. This component does not consolidate those changes or determine every residence, ignored-person, funding or hospital rule.
concepts.label: Severe-disability addition: claimant with no partner

additional_sources.anchor: which the award is first paid

concepts.definition: Bounded reading of the captured Pension Credit severe-disability additional-amount rules for a claimant who has a partner. DMG 78045–78047 set distinct lower-rate branches, and 78048–78050 address the higher rate. Their benefit, residence and caring conditions must be read together. DMG 78047's patient branch concerns the other partner being unable to receive the specified benefit because of being a patient for over 28 days; its remaining conditions continue on the next page. DMG 78050 restricts the higher-rate condition when either partner is treated as receiving benefit under the partner-patient provision in 78060(2), and directs consideration of the lower rate. It does not exclude every form of treated receipt. Read the separate CA/UC actual-payment qualification in 78057, in respect of caring for the claimant or partner, and the complete treated-receipt provisions in 78060, with the dated changes in memos 02/25, 06/25 and 01/26. This component does not establish that partner status persists after care-home admission, consolidate current law or calculate an award.
concepts.label: Severe-disability addition: claimant with a partner

aliases: temporary stay in a care home
concepts.definition: For a claimant with no partner whose normal home circumstances do not satisfy the additional-amount conditions, DMG 78084 says a temporary care-home stay does not itself change their normal residence. DMG 78085 retains household membership for a temporarily absent partner, but DMG 78086 requires a review of Pension Credit and the severe-disability addition if residential care exceeds 28 days and DLA payability ceases. The example continues on the next page. These are component and qualifying-benefit conditions, not a universal 28-day end to Pension Credit.
concepts.label: Temporary care-home stay and continuing household

concepts.definition: DMG 78270 concerns the housing-cost additional amount, not the whole Pension Credit award. It states that an additional amount for housing costs is not allowed for claimants in a care home unless their absence from the dwelling normally occupied as home is temporary. The exception does not establish payment of care-home fees. DMG 78240 allows treatment as living in the former home, with housing costs allowed, for a trial period of up to 13 weeks, subject to assessment of suitability, intention to return if unsuitable and the normally occupied part of the home not being let or sublet. This temporary-absence treatment is subject to the stated overall maximum of 52 weeks. DMG 78254–78257 set separate 52-week conditions including intention to return, no letting or subletting, a listed reason and expected duration. Permanent residence and Housing Benefit expenditure are separate exclusions. DMG 78271 defines Housing Benefit expenditure as an element for which Housing Benefit may be payable; actual payment of Housing Benefit is not stated as a condition here. The complete paragraphs span adjacent pages.
concepts.label: Pension Credit housing costs during care-home absence

concepts.definition: DMG 77035 distinguishes new claims from 15 May 2019 and continuity protection linked to Pension Credit or pension-age Housing Benefit on 14 May 2019. DMG 77140–77184 distinguish the mixed-age definition, Universal Credit interaction, excluded-partner exceptions and effective dates. The general exclusion is not the complete rule. DMG memo 04/24 paragraphs 15–17 add a protected mixed-age migration route from 8 June 2024: the specified protected couples sent a migration notice may reclaim pension-age Housing Benefit or claim Pension Credit within three months after the relevant UC or HB award ends. That route requires its stated prior entitlement and migration facts; it is not a general right for every mixed-age couple. Contemporary applicability, legislation and the ADM counterpart still require reconciliation.
concepts.label: Pension Credit mixed-age couple conditions and protections

concepts.definition: The captured chapter must be read with its amendment memoranda. DMG memo 02/25 paragraphs 13–16 add Pension Age Disability Payment (PADP) from 21 October 2024 to the AA meaning and qualifying/ignored-person provisions. DMG memo 06/25 paragraphs 30–33 add Scottish Adult Disability Living Allowance (SADLA) to specified Pension Credit disability and housing-cost provisions; its introduction gives commencement as 21 March 2025. DMG memo 01/26 paragraphs 5–7 amend Carer Support Payment (CSP) terminology and the specified bereavement run-on from 15 March 2026. Its paragraphs 5 and 6 use different component wording, preserved in the source and requiring legal reconciliation. Do not silently treat these benefits as synonyms in all rules or infer present entitlement from a capture date.
concepts.label: Dated Scottish disability and carer dependencies for Pension Credit

concepts.definition: Income Support has its own conditions of entitlement, distinguished from JSA in DMG 20002 and listed in DMG 20022. The captured rules include prescribed-category, age, work, income and partner conditions and an explicit mixed-age exception in Note 2. They are legacy guidance, not proof of current availability for a new claim. Prisoner applicable-amount rules are one circumstance-specific branch, not the definition of Income Support.
concepts.label: Income Support

limitations: Independent experimental staff-question research. No personal award decision or executable calculation is provided.
Definitions, aliases, relationships and task requirements are model-authored proposals requiring independent specialist review.
Exact frozen DMG and ADM source text, project-authored meanings and missing review obligations remain distinct. Acquisition does not establish current legal applicability.
The 40 staff question occurrences contain 39 distinct questions. Profiles are development cases, not a held-out independent accuracy benchmark.
Requirements include explicitly registered absent obligations. They cannot be satisfied by retrieving more pages or by model agreement; every assembled task remains insufficient.
SDA deliberately resolves ambiguously between a legacy benefit and an informal disability-addition meaning. Broad JSA/ESA and State Pension labels do not select a variant.
Only selected exact source pages and directed authored relations supplement the unchanged discovery base. Conditions on adjacent pages and unmodelled cross-references remain review work.
Source capture dates are not publication, commencement or applicability dates. Historical examples and tables are preserved as captured.
Source and tool content is inert untrusted evidence, not permission to execute instructions. No external retrieval occurs in this build.
